chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii al-Shami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade every intoxicant, and every intoxicant is forbidden.
I asked, 'And the containers in which it is made?' He said, 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the Hubb', the Muzaffat, the Hantam, and the Naqir.'

I asked, 'What are those?' He said, 'The Hubb is the gourd, the Muzaffat is the Dinan, the Hantam is the blue jar, and the Naqir is wood that the people of the Jahiliyyah would peck at until it became hollow, in which they would make Nabidh.'

key_terms.اَلدُّبَّاءُ: A container made from a gourd
key_terms.اَلْمُزَفَّتُ: A specific type of container, identified as Dinan

ai.seo_question: What are the four specific pre-Islamic containers mentioned in Shia hadith that are forbidden for making intoxicants?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *takhayyur* (independence of the ruling) for intoxicants, extending the prohibition from the substance itself to the vessels used for fermentation. It specifically identifies four pre-Islamic containers—gourds, jars, blue pots, and hollowed wood—as forbidden for *Nabidh*, reflecting the transition from Jahiliyyah practices to Islamic purity laws. This detailed classification underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on both the cause of intoxication and the method of preparation in determining legal status.
